correctness.rationale: The exact rJR violation equivalence holds with weak threshold inequality. A top-two committee failure produces a missing candidate with unrepresented support at most n-1 and quality at least n/[2(n-1)]. If its quality is subunit, strict-majority support makes pairing it with the top candidate rJR. If it is unit-quality, a separate exact-half argument produces a quality-two rJR pair. The ratio algebra is monotone in the relevant parameters, and the three-candidate construction meets all equalities. Equality rigidity is derived from the proof. Exact-integer exhaustive and extremal checks using the embedded checker.cpp passed. These finite checks do not imply arbitrary-size correctness; the analytic proof does.

value.rationale: The price of fairness is a central benchmark in the cited paper. For the first nontrivial committee size, this theorem gives the exact finite-voter price for every n and arbitrary supported candidate count, showing an explicit 4/[3(3n-2)] improvement over the unrestricted global price and identifying the support geometry needed at equality. This is a natural missing non-asymptotic invariant, not an arbitrary finite census, routine parameter renaming, or a new claim to a known lower-bound example.
